newsitem.title: FRANCE: British Airways appeals on Kuwait hostages ruling.
newsitem.headline: British Airways appeals on Kuwait hostages ruling.

text.p: British Airways launched an appeal in a French court on Monday against a ruling that it should compensate 61 Gulf War hostages for landing them in Iraqi hands in occupied Kuwait, an airline spokeswoman said.

The 61 French nationals and foreign residents of France were among the 364 people on board a BA flight from London which landed at Kuwait airport on August 2, 1990 -- four hours after Iraqi invaders entered the emirate.

BA lawyer Fernard Garnault outlined the company's case before a Paris appeals court as it battled a lower court ruling in November ordering it to pay the hostages 400,000 to 600,000 francs ($80,000 to $120,000) each in damages, according to the time they spent in captivity.
The plaintiffs charge that BA had committed a "severe error" and demanded compensation for the mental anguish they suffered.
Iraqi soldiers seized the Boeing 747, and its passengers were held hostage for up to three months, some being used as human shields against allied bombing of strategic Iraqi sites.
BA denies the plaintiffs' allegation that the flight landed at Kuwait to drop off 15 undercover British Special Air Service Regiment (SAS) commandos who boarded at the last minute.

"Garnault explained that BA had no way of knowing that an invation of Kuwait was about to happen," the spokeswoman said. "The act of war surprised the whole world and we had no reason to think that we could not land," she quoted him as saying.
The lawyer pointed out that the hostages had already been paid compensation of around 30,000 francs ($6,000) each out of a French state fund set up for victims of terrorist or similar attacks.
"The lawyer denied that there was an SAS team on board. That is fit for a novel, no one boarded the plane between its scheduled departure time and the time it left," the spokeswoman said.
The Paris court will give its judgement on November 12.
The French government has joined the ex-hostages in demanding that the airline reimburse its guarantee fund and pay additional damages.
